name: CEC-120 COMPETITION CASE
what_this_is: The complete set of inputs needed to reproduce the CEC-120 case exactly as
the submitted film shows it. One file, so that the inputs live in one place
instead of being restated in a script.
source document  +  engineer decisions  ->  production API  ->  result
Everything under `inputs` is on the left of that arrow: a document somebody
wrote, and decisions a person made. Nothing under `inputs` is a result.
`expected_results` is on the RIGHT of the arrow and is NEVER fed back in.
It exists so a reproduction can be compared against the film, and it is
read only after the run has finished. If a figure there and a figure the
pipeline computes ever disagree, the pipeline is right and this file is

inputs.production_requirements_brief: We need a new electronics assembly line. The product goes through assembly, screwdriving, inspection and packaging. We need about 1,900 units per day. The available production area is 30 by 18 meters. We have eight operators. We would prefer not to buy unnecessary equipment.
inputs.improvement_request: We need 1900 units/day. Avoid buying new machines if possible.
_note_on_the_brief: The target, floor area and headcount inside the brief are the CUSTOMER's
own words, typed by the operator exactly as the document states them.
They are inputs, not expected results: the pipeline re-attributes them to
CUSTOMER because the source states them, and only the shift pattern

_why: The rule table has no rule that turns 'the enclosure is moulded in ABS'
or 'a product identification label' into a station, and Fabrivium
refuses to invent one. An engineer says which operation handles each,
and the decision is recorded against that operation.
These links resolve coverage. They set no cycle time and change no
simulation input, so they cannot move a throughput figure.
coverage_links.component.label: Packaging

_why: How the engineer described each station to the estimator. Only one
station is not MANUAL, and it is the single most consequential input in
Screw fastening is ASSISTED — a driver on a balancer rather than a hand
screwdriver — which the estimator prices at 39.8 s against 48.0 s for
the same six screws done by hand. At 48 s screwdriving is the slowest
station on the line and becomes the constraint; at 39.8 s it is not, and
the constraint sits on the two cable connections where the film shows
it. Omitting this line reproduces a 1,196/day baseline, which is a
correct answer to a different question.

engineer_decisions.reason: Not stated in the brief; this line runs two shifts.
Not stated in the brief; this line runs 8-hour shifts.
Engineer override of Fabrivium's 38.5 s estimate for the two cable connections.
_why_not_a_starting_value: The film shows the estimate produced first and the override typed
after it, in that order. Starting the station at 40 s would erase the
override and quietly promote an engineer's judgement into a source
fact — which is the exact failure the provenance model exists to

_when: Entered AFTER the strategies exist, so the recommended plan is seen
moving from 'nothing priced yet' to cost-complete. Pre-seeding it
would remove the moment that makes the cost claim checkable.

accepted_cycle_times_seconds._note: Estimator output, plus the one engineer override. Listed so a reproduction can be diffed station by station rather than only on the headline.

how_to_reproduce: cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app        # a live server, not TestClient
The script reads this file for every input above and prints each computed
figure next to its expected_results counterpart.
